prompt:
INSTRUCTIONS OF ROLE
You are a GENERATOR OF CORPORATE SCENARIOS that are realistic and auditable for dataset creation.
Your objective is to produce:
1. a PROJECT_PACK (project dossier) and
2. a BLUEPRINT (Slack channel script)
   that will be used by another model to simulate Slack-style conversations.
   You will NOT see anything beyond what is in this prompt. Do NOT assume external context.

CRITICAL OUTPUT RESTRICTION (VERY IMPORTANT)
* Return ONLY 1 valid JSON object (with no text outside the JSON).
* Do not use markdown fences (```).
* DO NOT use literal line breaks inside strings. If needed, use \n or if it is a tab use \t.
* Do not invent keys outside the schema.
* Ensure quotes and braces are closed.
* DO NOT “echo” inputs: do not repeat run_meta, affinity_band, nor copy fields from participants_json to the output.
  You may only repeat: the _id (to identify the person) and the selected role.

CONSISTENCY OBJECTIVE (why we are being strict)
This JSON will be consumed by code and by other prompts. Consistent outputs reduce parsing errors and variability.

GLOSSARY / DEFINITIONS (use as internal reference; DO NOT return this text)
* participant: simulated person identified by _id; do not use proper names.
* ESCO title: trajectory titles already normalized; you must select the role from these titles (without inventing a job title).
* PROJECT_PACK:
  * project: project definition (title, objective, deliverables, constraints, stakeholders, risks, timeline)
  * themes: recurring topics that naturally appear in conversations
  * backlog: trackable tasks with task-coherent title, and scope coherent to the project
  * artifacts: citable things in Slack (doc, spreadsheet, ticket, checklist, guideline etc.)
* BLUEPRINT:
  * channel_name_hint: channel name suggestion
  * threads_plan: threads (TH1..) and what must happen in each one
  * mandatory_decisions: mandatory decisions that must appear in the conversation
  * artifacts_to_reference: artifacts/tasks that must be cited in the thread
  * talk_distribution_by_role: share of speech by role (floats summing ~1.0) (All participants must speak, even if very little)
  * channel_rituals: channel rituals (e.g.: async standup, weekly checkpoint, review, postmortem)

INPUT
You will receive:
* affinity_band: HIGH|MID|LOW   (use ONLY to calibrate style; do not return it in the output)
* participants_json: list of participants, each with:
  {
  "_id": int,
  "trajectory_lastK": [string],              # ESCO titles (short list, in chronological order)
  "trajectory_summary": string,              # consolidated summary (may contain “->”)
  "skills_text": string,                     # aggregated skills
  }

DETERMINISTIC RULE FOR role (WITHOUT INVENTING A JOB TITLE)
For each participant, define role with the following priority (first that exists):
role is either the last element of the trajectory, or the most frequent job title in the trajectories.
IMPORTANT: Do not create abbreviations (“PM”, “QA”) if this is NOT in the ESCO titles received.

TASK
The project and each task must be plausible for the role (scope, seniority, and work context). Do not assign technical construction/implementation to non-technical roles (e.g.: sales assistant, doorman, cook); in those cases, focus on day-to-day activities (processes, routines, service, operational improvement, standardization, quality). If there are very distinct roles, design an inter-area project where each role contributes within its scope (e.g.: one defines rules/process and another implements; or one team performs on-site activities while another provides support with guidance). Tasks can be on-site/operational and do not need to always generate artifacts; keep artifacts only when it makes sense (they can be light, like checklist, schedule, script, guide, or record).
1. For each participant: produce { _id, role } using the deterministic rule above.
2. Create a single, coherent PROJECT_PACK (generic enough for multiple areas, but concrete and coherent with the scope of the job role, whether management, product development, software, establish business rules, research, etc; it can be of any scope, including in-person work roles like kitchen, it can be a project for planning a new menu, restaurant model, etc; think of some theme for them to discuss).
   * project:
     * title: short (<= 80 chars)
     * objective: 1–2 sentences (<= 220 chars)
     * deliverables: 3–6 items
     * constraints: 3–6 items (deadlines, compliance, technical/process limitations)
     * stakeholders: 3–6 roles (not names)
     * deadline_days: integer
       * if run_meta.timebox_days exists and >0, use that value;
       * otherwise use a plausible value between 7 and 30.
     * risks: 2–5 (each with mitigation)
   * themes: 3–6 (theme + why_relevant <= 140 chars)
   * backlog: 5–12 tasks T1..T12 with owner_role (must be an existing role in participants.role) and definition_of_done
   * artifacts: 4–8 artifacts A1..A8 with type and used_for (<= 140 chars)
3. Create a BLUEPRINT for the Slack channel:
   * threads_plan: 3–6 threads TH1..TH6
     * thread_goal (<= 140 chars)
     * trigger (<= 120 chars)
     * target_messages_range: [min,max] (use plausible ranges, e.g.: [15,25])
     * mandatory_decisions: 1–3 per thread, with decision_id D1..D8 (unique overall)
     * artifacts_to_reference: list A* and/or T* relevant to that thread
   * talk_distribution_by_role: shares (floats) summing ~1.0, using existing roles
   * channel_rituals: 2–5 rituals

STYLE RULES BY AFFINITY (use internally; do not return affinity_band)
* HIGH: more jargon and shorthand; fast decisions; fewer clarifications.
* MID: balance.
* LOW: more checks and clarifications, higher chance of rework.

GENERAL CONSTRAINTS
* Do not use proper names, emails, companies, specific locations.
* Corporate language applicable to product/tech/ops/data/customer service.
* Do not include personal metrics or human evaluations. Only project details.

OUTPUT JSON SCHEMA (MINIMUM OUTPUT — DO NOT ECHO INPUTS)
{
  "participants": [
    {"_id": 0, "role": "..."}
  ],
  "project_pack": {
    "project": {
      "title": "...",
      "objective": "...",
      "deliverables": ["..."],
      "constraints": ["..."],
      "stakeholders": ["..."],
      "deadline_days": 0,
      "risks": [{"risk": "...", "mitigation": "..."}]
    },
    "themes": [{"theme": "...", "why_relevant": "..."}],
    "backlog": [{"task_id": "T1", "task": "...", "owner_role": "...", "definition_of_done": ["..."]}],
    "artifacts": [{"artifact_id": "A1", "type": "doc|sheet|ticket|checklist|guideline|incident|other", "title": "...", "used_for": "..."}]
  },
  "blueprint": {
    "channel_name_hint": "...",
    "threads_plan": [{
      "thread_id": "TH1",
      "thread_goal": "...",
      "trigger": "...",
      "target_messages_range": [15, 25],
      "mandatory_decisions": [{"decision_id": "D1", "decision": "..."}],
      "artifacts_to_reference": ["A1","T2"]
    }],
    "talk_distribution_by_role": [{"role": "...", "share": 0.0}],
    "channel_rituals": ["..."]
  }
}

FINAL
Return only the JSON in the schema above.

HIGH

1. a PROJECT_PACK (project dossier) and

   You will NOT see anything beyond what is in this prompt. Do NOT assume external context.

CRITICAL OUTPUT RESTRICTION (VERY IMPORTANT)
* Return ONLY 1 valid JSON object (with no text outside the JSON).
* Do not use markdown fences (```).
* DO NOT use literal line breaks inside strings. If needed, use \n or if it is a tab use \t.
* Do not invent keys outside the schema.
* Ensure quotes and braces are closed.
* DO NOT “echo” inputs: do not repeat run_meta, affinity_band, nor copy fields from participants_json to the output.

CONSISTENCY OBJECTIVE (why we are being strict)
This JSON will be consumed by code and by other prompts. Consistent outputs reduce parsing errors and variability.

GLOSSARY / DEFINITIONS (use as internal reference; DO NOT return this text)
* participant: simulated person identified by _id; do not use proper names.
* ESCO title: trajectory titles already normalized; you must select the role from these titles (without inventing a job title).
* PROJECT_PACK:
  * project: project definition (title, objective, deliverables, constraints, stakeholders, risks, timeline)
  * themes: recurring topics that naturally appear in conversations
  * backlog: trackable tasks with task-coherent title, and scope coherent to the project
  * artifacts: citable things in Slack (doc, spreadsheet, ticket, checklist, guideline etc.)
* BLUEPRINT:
  * channel_name_hint: channel name suggestion
  * threads_plan: threads (TH1..) and what must happen in each one
  * mandatory_decisions: mandatory decisions that must appear in the conversation
  * artifacts_to_reference: artifacts/tasks that must be cited in the thread
  * talk_distribution_by_role: share of speech by role (floats summing ~1.0) (All participants must speak, even if very little)

* affinity_band: HIGH|MID|LOW   (use ONLY to calibrate style; do not return it in the output)

  "_id": int,
  "trajectory_lastK": [string],              # ESCO titles (short list, in chronological order)
  "trajectory_summary": string,              # consolidated summary (may contain “->”)
  "skills_text": string,                     # aggregated skills
  }

DETERMINISTIC RULE FOR role (WITHOUT INVENTING A JOB TITLE)
For each participant, define role with the following priority (first that exists):
role is either the last element of the trajectory, or the most frequent job title in the trajectories.
IMPORTANT: Do not create abbreviations (“PM”, “QA”) if this is NOT in the ESCO titles received.

TASK
The project and each task must be plausible for the role (scope, seniority, and work context). Do not assign technical construction/implementation to non-technical roles (e.g.: sales assistant, doorman, cook); in those cases, focus on day-to-day activities (processes, routines, service, operational improvement, standardization, quality). If there are very distinct roles, design an inter-area project where each role contributes within its scope (e.g.: one defines rules/process and another implements; or one team performs on-site activities while another provides support with guidance). Tasks can be on-site/operational and do not need to always generate artifacts; keep artifacts only when it makes sense (they can be light, like checklist, schedule, script, guide, or record).
1. For each participant: produce { _id, role } using the deterministic rule above.
2.      * title: short (<= 80 chars)

     * deliverables: 3–6 items

     * stakeholders: 3–6 roles (not names)

   * talk_distribution_by_role: shares (floats) summing ~1.0, using existing roles
